about: Common Shade's shared health and equity taxonomy, used by the plan workbook (/plan/), the Solutions library, the heat action plan provision review, Follow the money and Signals, and the health and equity pages. Three dimensions kept apart: who and where (people), what is provided (provisions) and how far it is shown (status). A record that mentions a group does not thereby provide anything for it; a provision on paper is not delivery; a service open to all is not equitable access. Labels describe; none certifies anything as safe or equitable. tools/equity-taxonomy.js loads and checks this file.

people.label: Pregnant and postpartum people
people.definition: People who are pregnant or have recently given birth.
people.include: The record names pregnancy, the postpartum period or maternal health.
people.exclude: General references to women or families.
examples: Heat and pregnancy guidance for health workers
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Newborns and children
people.definition: Babies, children and young people, at home, in school or in care.
people.include: The record names newborns, infants, children, students or schools.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Older people
people.definition: People in later life, including those living alone.
people.include: The record names older people or the elderly.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Disabled people
people.definition: People with physical, sensory, intellectual or psychosocial disabilities.
people.include: The record names disability or accessibility for disabled people.
people.exclude: Health conditions not described as disability.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Informal, contract and piece-rate workers
people.definition: People paid by the day, by the piece or without a formal contract.
people.include: The record names informal, casual, day-wage, contract, gig or piece-rate work, or street vending.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Home-based workers
people.definition: People who earn from work done in their own home.
people.include: The record names home-based work, homeworkers or work done at home for pay.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Tenants
people.definition: People renting their home, who may not be able to change the building.
people.include: The record names tenants, renters or landlords.
examples: A renter who cannot add roof insulation
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Migrant workers
people.definition: People working away from where they are from, within or across borders.
people.include: The record names migrant or seasonal migrant workers.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: Paid and unpaid caregivers
people.definition: People who care for children, older or disabled people, paid or unpaid.
people.include: The record names care work, caregivers, carers or care responsibilities.
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

people.label: People facing gender-related exclusion
people.definition: Women, transgender and gender-diverse people where gender shapes access, safety or control.
people.include: The record names gender, women or gendered access, safety or control.
people.exclude: A mention of households, which does not show who in the household benefits.
examples: Who controls a household's cooling spending
people.evidence: The record's own words name the group.

provisions.label: Earnings protection
provisions.definition: People do not lose pay or work by using the protection: paid breaks, income support or cash in heat.
provisions.include: The arrangement itself pays, compensates or protects earnings.
provisions.exclude: Saying earnings matter, or that income loss is a risk.
provisions.evidence: A passage in the record or a checked source that describes the payment or guarantee.

provisions.label: Work-rest coverage
provisions.definition: Rest, changed hours or lighter loads in heat, and who they cover.
provisions.include: The arrangement sets rest, schedules or workload in heat.
provisions.evidence: A passage describing the rule or arrangement.

provisions.label: Water, sanitation and privacy
provisions.definition: Drinking water, toilets and private, safe facilities people can actually use.
provisions.include: The arrangement provides water, toilets, washing or privacy.
provisions.exclude: Advice to drink water without provision.

provisions.label: Accessible services and cooling
provisions.definition: Cooling or support that disabled, older and other intended users can reach and use: step-free, nearby, open when needed, with dependants welcome.
provisions.include: The arrangement addresses physical access, distance, opening hours or transport.
examples: Step-free cooling centre open in the evening
provisions.evidence: A passage describing the access arrangement.

provisions.label: Care-service continuity
provisions.definition: Childcare, eldercare, disability support and health services keep running through heat, without moving the work onto unpaid carers.
provisions.include: The arrangement keeps a care or health service running in heat.

provisions.label: Tenant protections
provisions.definition: People who rent can benefit without rent rises, eviction or needing a landlord's permission they cannot get.
provisions.include: The arrangement addresses rent, tenure or landlord permission.
provisions.exclude: Housing improvements with no word on tenure.

provisions.label: Confidential, non-punitive reporting
provisions.definition: People can report symptoms or barriers privately, without losing pay or work, and someone responds.
provisions.include: The arrangement sets a reporting channel with protection from retaliation or a named responder.
examples: Anonymous heat complaints with a named inspector
provisions.evidence: A passage describing the channel and its protection.

provisions.label: Participation in decisions
provisions.definition: Intended users can shape or challenge how the protection works: committees with real say, worker or community voice in budgets and rules.
provisions.include: The arrangement gives users a role in decisions.
provisions.exclude: Consultation alone, or a seat without a say.
provisions.evidence: A passage describing the role and what it can change.

provisions.label: Operational funding
provisions.definition: Money for running, staffing and maintaining the protection, not only for building it.
provisions.include: The arrangement names recurring or operating funds.
provisions.evidence: A passage or source naming the funding.

provisions.label: Maternal and newborn provisions
provisions.definition: Arrangements that address pregnancy, postpartum and newborn needs: accommodation at work, antenatal care access, facility readiness.
provisions.include: The arrangement provides something for pregnant or postpartum people or newborns.
provisions.exclude: Naming pregnant people as at risk.
examples: Cool waiting areas in antenatal clinics

status.label: Explicitly documented
status.definition: The record or document states the provision as part of the arrangement, with a quoted passage.

status.label: Partly documented or general mention
status.definition: The issue is named, but without a concrete action, a responsible body or resources.

status.label: Not found in reviewed material
status.definition: The material reviewed was read for this and did not contain it. Says nothing about practice or other documents.

status.label: Not assessed
status.definition: Nobody has reviewed this yet. Not a negative finding.

status.label: Document inaccessible or unreadable
status.definition: The document could not be opened or its text could not be read reliably.

status.label: Reported implemented
status.definition: The implementer or a news source reports delivery; not independently evaluated.

status.label: Outcome evaluated
status.definition: An independent evaluation reports effects; see its scope and limits.
